questions.explanation: cellular telephone: A low-power portable radio that communicates through an interconnected series of repeater stations called cells.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: A low-power portable radio that communicates through an interconnected series of repeater stations called cells.

questions.explanation: A cellular telephone is a low-power radio that communicates through an interconnected series of repeater stations called cells, handing the call off as you move. A base station is fixed hardware at one location; a scanner only receives and cycles through channels; a repeater rebroadcasts one signal on a second frequency.
questions.question: Driving across town, your portable phone never loses its signal. Without you doing anything, it hands the call off from one low-power repeater site to the next as you move. This works because the phone is a:

questions.explanation: interoperable communications system: A communication system that uses voice-over-Internet Protocol (VoIP) technology to allow multiple agencies to share data, voice, and other forms of communication in a disaster or emergency situation.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: A communication system that uses voice-over-Internet Protocol (VoIP) technology to allow multiple agencies to share data, voice, and other forms of communication in a disaster or emergency situation.

questions.explanation: An interoperable communications system uses voice-over-Internet Protocol (VoIP) technology so multiple agencies can share voice, data, and other communication in a disaster. Trunking only assigns frequencies within one system; paging sends alerts; telemetry transmits patient data.
questions.question: At a tornado disaster, fire, EMS, and law enforcement crews from three counties can all talk to each other and share data, even though each agency normally uses its own system. The shared system that links them uses Internet-based voice technology and is called:

questions.explanation: emotional intelligence: The ability to understand and manage one’s own emotions and properly respond to the emotions of others.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: The ability to understand and manage one’s own emotions and properly respond to the emotions of others.

questions.explanation: Understanding and managing your own emotions, and responding well to the emotions of others, is emotional intelligence. Rapport is the trusting relationship you build with a patient; facilitation is encouraging a patient to keep talking; ethnocentrism is treating your own culture as more important than another's.
questions.question: After a rough call, your partner snaps at you over something small. You feel your own temper rising, recognize it, take a breath, and answer calmly instead of snapping back. What have you just used?

questions.explanation: health information exchange: A system that allows EMS providers to access relevant health data (eg, past medical problems, medications, allergies, end-of-life decisions), avoid duplicating unnecessary tests, and ensure that the information needed to provide care is available.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: A system that allows EMS providers to access relevant health data (eg, past medical problems, medications, allergies, end-of-life decisions), avoid duplicating unnecessary tests, and ensure that the information needed to provide care is available.

questions.explanation: A health information exchange is the shared system that lets providers access a patient's health data - past problems, medications, allergies - and avoid duplicating tests. The mobile data terminal is only the screen in the ambulance that displays the information; the patient care report is the legal record your crew creates for this call.
questions.question: Before you arrive, the screen in your ambulance pulls up a frequent patient's medication list, allergies, and past medical problems from records shared between hospitals and EMS agencies, so you do not repeat tests she had yesterday. The system that supplied this information is a:

questions.explanation: patient care report: The legal document used to record all patient care activities. This report has direct patient care functions and administrative and quality control functions.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: The legal document used to record all patient care activities. This report has direct patient care functions and administrative and quality control functions.

questions.explanation: The patient care report is the legal document used to record all patient care activities, with direct care, administrative, and quality control functions. A radio report and a handover are spoken communications; the dispatch log records response times, not patient care.
questions.question: Months from now, this call may be reviewed in court and by your agency's quality team. One document will follow the patient as the official legal record of everything your crew did. That document is the:

questions.explanation: base station: Any radio hardware containing a transmitter and receiver that is located in a fixed place.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: Any radio hardware containing a transmitter and receiver that is located in a fixed place.

questions.explanation: A base station is radio hardware containing a transmitter and receiver located in a fixed place - headquarters. A repeater's job is narrower: it receives a signal on one frequency and rebroadcasts it on a second frequency; a scanner only receives; a cellular telephone is a low-power portable.
questions.question: Every transmission from your crews funnels through the powerful transmitter and receiver mounted at headquarters, which never moves and coordinates the whole system's traffic. That fixed installation is the:
